blocks.text: In verses 4–11, the servant speaks as one taught by the Lord, enduring abuse without turning back and relying on the Lord’s help. Isaiah’s servant language elsewhere can refer to Jacob or Israel and to a plural community, while singular servant poems such as this one also invite individual readings. The passage itself does not settle whether this voice is individual, collective, prophetic, royal, or messianic, so readers should hold those possibilities with care.

The Great Isaiah Scroll preserves an almost complete witness to all sixty-six chapters of Isaiah. It broadly aligns with the Masoretic tradition while also containing many spelling and substantive differences; other Qumran Isaiah manuscripts and interpretive writings likewise show that Isaiah was actively copied, transmitted, and interpreted.
